goal:
Create a single self-contained file index.html implementing an interactive full-viewport HTML5 Canvas orbital particle simulation in dark space (#060913):
1. Responsive full-window <canvas> using requestAnimationFrame and devicePixelRatio scaling.
2. Central glowing star using createRadialGradient and a subtle corona pulse.
3. At least 5 orbiting planets with distinct orbital radii, speeds, colors, at least 3 moons/satellites, and fading orbital trails.
4. Twinkling background starfield with at least 150 stars.
5. Interactive glassmorphism HUD overlay with:
   - Play/Pause toggle button
   - Trails ON/OFF toggle button
   - Reset button
   - Speed range slider (<input type="range" min="0.2" max="3.0" step="0.1" value="1.0">) with live multiplier readout
   - Live FPS, simulation time (s), and active burst particle count
6. Clicking anywhere on the canvas spawns a radial burst of glowing particles with velocity damping and fade-out.
Keep everything self-contained in index.html with zero external dependencies and valid JavaScript syntax.
constraints: the canvas has id="sky" and is sized to innerWidth x innerHeight times devicePixelRatio
the buttons have ids btnPlay, btnTrails, btnReset
btnPlay reads "Pause" while playing and "Play" while paused
btnTrails reads "Trails ON" or "Trails OFF"
the slider is <input type="range" id="speed" min="0.2" max="3.0" step="0.1" value="1.0">
the element id="speedVal" shows the multiplier with one decimal, like "1.0x"
the readouts have ids fps, simTime, bursts
simTime shows seconds with one decimal and the unit, like "12.3 s"
scale = Math.min(W, H) / 700 multiplies every orbit radius and every body size
orbits are ellipses centered on the canvas with y radius = 0.62 x the x radius
there are six planets with orbit radii 62, 98, 140, 186, 246, 304
the planet periods are 4.2, 7, 10.5, 15, 24, 36 seconds
the planet sizes are 4.5, 6.5, 7.5, 5.5, 13, 9
the planet colors are #ff9b6b, #7be0a4, #5fb4ff, #e2674e, #e6c288, #a58bff
the moons per planet are 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 1, which makes 7 moons
the fifth planet has a tilted ring drawn with ctx.ellipse
each orbit is stroked as an ellipse with strokeStyle rgba(130, 160, 220, 0.11) and lineWidth 1
planet glow is a radial gradient of radius 3 x size from color + "55" to color + "00"
the planet disc gradient starts from an inner circle centered at (x - 0.35 * size, y - 0.35 * size)
the planet disc gradient stops are #ffffff at 0, the planet color at 0.25, #0a0f1f at 1
each trail keeps the last 90 positions of its planet
trails are drawn as line segments with lineCap "round" in the planet color, oldest first
trail segment lineWidth = Math.max(0.6, size * scale * 0.42 * i / n)
trail segment globalAlpha = (i / n) * 0.55
the star core has radius 24 * scale and gradient stops #fffbe6 at 0, #ffd76a at 0.45, #ff8a2b at 1
the star corona has radius 5.2 x the core and fades from rgba(255, 214, 130, 0.55) to transparent
the corona radius is multiplied by pulse = 1 + 0.07 * Math.sin(1.7 * t)
there are 180 background stars with radius between 0.3 and 1.6 px
star alpha = base + 0.28 * Math.sin(t * rate + phase)
about one star in five is tinted rgb(255, 214, 170) and about one in three rgb(170, 205, 255)
a click on the canvas spawns 46 to 64 particles over a full circle of directions
particle speed is between 70 and 280 px per second
particle velocity is multiplied by Math.pow(0.12, dt) every frame
each particle has its own decay between 0.45 and 1.0, set at spawn, and its life falls by decay * dt
particles are drawn with globalCompositeOperation "lighter" as radial gradients of radius 3 x their size
particle color is hsla(hue, 100%, 75%, life) and a particle is removed when life <= 0
the HUD panel has position fixed, top 16px, left 16px, width 248px
the HUD background is rgba(18, 28, 54, 0.42) with backdrop-filter blur(14px)
the HUD border is 1px solid rgba(140, 180, 255, 0.22) with border-radius 14px
the HUD title is uppercase with letter-spacing
the three buttons share one flex row and their text never wraps (white-space: nowrap)
the three readouts sit in a two-column grid with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums
the frame delta is capped at 0.05 seconds
simulation time advances by delta * speed only while playing
planet starting phases are fixed numbers, i * 1.37 + 0.4, never Math.random()
Reset sets the time to 0, empties trails and bursts and restores the starting phases
